question: What cathode does the anode-free full cell use, how is it prepared so that the cell contains no sodium metal on assembly, and what cathode capacity was assumed for its energy density?
rendered:
The anode-free full cell uses a pre-sodiated pyrite cathode. The cathode is prepared by assembling a pre-sodiated pyrite cathode with a carbon nucleation layer on the current collector. The carbon nucleation layer is prepared by depositing conductive carbon black and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose on the Al foil using aqueous processing. The pyrite (FeS2) cathode is also processed in a similar fashion using pyrite, carbon black, and CMC on Al foil. The pre-sodiation of the pyrite cathode is not described in detail in the document.

The energy density of the full cell is calculated based on the mass of the presodiated pyrite cathode and the carbon nucleation layer. The cathode capacity is not explicitly stated in the document, but it is mentioned that the presodiated pyrite cathode has a capacity of 335 mAh/g. The energy density is calculated to be approximately 400 Wh/kg.
